# Released recording workflow observations

[Native screenshot capture](screenshot-capture-evidence.md) adds 24 actual released picker/process/file workflows, including the real 180-second deadline. Four additional faults cover dropped callers/owners, stubborn descendants and a nonregular output file. Application attachment/editor ownership and stopping audio before awaiting the picker remain pending.

[Meeting recording and desktop ownership](../../../mluva-gtk/tests/fixtures/meeting-owner-evidence.md) adds fourteen actual released recorder-to-HTTP/archive transactions and nine application Meeting workflows/47 GTK states. The native recorder/session/readiness/retry and GTK owner now join real audio staging, archives and capture preferences. Additional cancellation/close faults protect untransferred audio and late publication. Complete root assembly and Meeting acceptance remain Pending.

[Earlier Meeting workflow evidence](../../../mluva-gtk/tests/fixtures/meeting-evidence.md) adds fifteen actual Scribe diarization/archive/retry workflows/23 states against unchanged release observations. Incognito erasure, failed private index saves, missing recordings and preserved retry identities match. A separate native in-flight request-drop fault erases owned finalized audio without a late archive write. Complete application lifecycle remains pending.

The immutable reference is Mluva 1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. Temporary comparison programs import the checksum-verified release archive outside maintained Rust sources and compare every imported workflow module with that commit. The frozen expected outputs come from the released application. Native tests neither import nor invoke Python.

`released-recording-workflows.json` contains 70 complete recording observations and the imported module digests. Its SHA-256 is `13c33ab98eb9f3816e2872878a8b7cc794f9e3d5dbcd5f129b5cf0ac15fec0dc`; the reference workflow digest is `e539145a529a1be6b0ba8a95c4108f470e5d5c2dafe44f14ec5e2457259bc44f`. Both implementations use real synthetic loopback multipart/SSE providers, native SQLite files and a real private X11 clipboard. The observer checks exact provider JSON and multipart fields/audio bytes, Raw Text versus prepared output, delivery receipts, complete persisted History rows, diagnostics, clipboard content and retained-file existence.

The cases cover scoped dictionaries, explicitly spoken snippets and frozen variable/rule values; Command with absent, empty, Unicode, boundary and oversized selections/instructions; optional cleanup/style success and controlled fallback; captured style instructions and explicit style removal; committed realtime text, invalid route metadata and one batch fallback; ElevenLabs/compatible batch transports; silence; automatic copy disabled; deferred continuation delivery; Incognito rejection/erasure and memory-only drafts; successful/failure audio retention; redacted provider failures; history/diagnostic write failures; retry-to-preview and current-rule reprocessing. Visual Command compares actual image bytes, capture timing and the context prompt. Terminal segment cleanup checks session/model/provider/raw coverage and ordered safe candidates. The [asynchronous producer](segment-cleanup-evidence.md) now adds 23 independently released sessions/26 projections and seven actual GTK capture transactions, including owned Codex children, bounded scheduling, safe fallback and exit cancellation.

Generated History UUIDs and timestamps are normalized. Audio paths become `$AUDIO`. Workflow/store wall-clock timings are compared for presence, not as performance measurements; supplied realtime duration still compares exactly at 188 ms. Source snapshot field names are adapted to the public native value types without changing expected outputs. Frozen-rule cases actually freeze the native store before editing it; explicit variable values are supplied identically to both clients.

The joined [GTK recording fixture](../../../mluva-gtk/tests/fixtures/released-recording-targets.json) adds seven complete workflows through real batch speech and a separate native GTK process. Its SHA-256 is `294c316962c3fbc664319e9f4698bbec9cbb5ac3d44ef2d6d68fdbd355051454`. Four captures insert once through the accessibility editing interface, including selected Entry/TextView ranges and Incognito; stale own-window focus copies without mutation; Command waits for review; Scratchpad keeps recoverable audio and waits for explicit delivery. The target process reports its own text, caret, selection, focus and edit count across every field. Both clients also compare actual clipboard bytes, History, provider requests and diagnostic outcomes. Generated target PIDs are omitted from the frozen output; the native test independently requires another process.

The target comparison uses `ATSPI_DISABLE_P2P=1` so the accessibility calls pass through the monitored private bus. Six workflows have no `GetText` calls. The explicit Command reads precisely `[7, 16]`; this positive control must be present, preventing a disconnected monitor from claiming content-free delivery. Default peer-to-peer transport, Wayland, broader editors and physical keys remain separate acceptance work.

The [diagnostics fixture](../../../mluva-core/tests/fixtures/released-diagnostics.json) freezes the released content-free SQLite schema, bounded retention, millisecond ties-to-even values, invalid-input rejection, chronological export and owner-only permissions. Its SHA-256 is `37a127965358c61fc15c95ecaafb6f0fe1320e959af37d367c258fe14dfd2dd8`. Export filenames and `generated_at` identify the same instant; this comparison failed before the native timestamp fix and passes after it. No provider alias, device label, user text or arbitrary exception payload appears in the exported metadata.

The explicit workflow tests require the repository's private display/network/PID/device runner, real `xclip`, and the built native target example. Run from the repository root with the platform development libraries and fixture dependencies available:

```sh
cargo build --locked -p mluva-gtk --example text_target_peer
bash dev/run-isolated-browser.sh tmp/recording-workflow -- cargo test --locked -p mluva-workflows --test recording -- --ignored --test-threads=1 --nocapture
bash dev/run-isolated-browser.sh tmp/recording-target -- cargo test --locked -p mluva-gtk --test recording_target -- --ignored --test-threads=1 --nocapture
```

The shared runner also checks its browser-tool prerequisites; these recording checks launch GTK targets and Openbox, without launching Firefox. It clears inherited credentials/compositor bindings, creates fresh session/accessibility buses and private data/config/home directories, hides host input/audio/GPU devices and isolates network/PID namespaces. Synthetic WAVs and provider responses stay inside that environment. Raw observations and logs remain private under ignored `tmp/`.

This milestone supplies production recording orchestration and its native target adapter. The [joined capture owner](../../../mluva-gtk/tests/fixtures/capture-lifecycle-evidence.md) now covers preparation, recording and realtime cleanup through the actual GTK page. Full application/service assembly and session/revision lifecycle, Live/review/continuation/meeting/archive controllers, screenshot capture/editor integration, global keys, D-Bus/widget lifecycle, packaging, final Python removal and whole-app performance remain pending. It is not a complete runnable native app and does not replace the installed 1.6.0 application.

[Application service evidence](application-services-evidence.md) adds eleven startup/recovery cases, 36 saved-settings transactions, six actual capture-factory transactions/two recordings and 28 title jobs. These invoke the native production store, factory, capture and title owners and compare independently frozen release outputs; complete application assembly remains pending.
